hook.en: A rectangle and a few circles can show at a glance how sets overlap. This picture was made popular by John Venn.
hook.kn: ಒಂದು ಆಯತ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಲವು ವೃತ್ತಗಳು ಗಣಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಒಮ್ಮೆಲೇ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದನ್ನು ಜಾನ್ ವೆನ್ ಜನಪ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸಿದರು.

say.en: A rectangle and a few circles can show at a glance how sets overlap. This picture was made popular by John Venn. In this lesson: Choose a universal set.
Draw and read Venn diagrams.

body.en: In a given context, the *universal set* $U$ is the basic set of which all the sets under study are subsets. For number problems we may take $U = R$ or $U = Z$; for a study of triangles, $U$ may be the set of all triangles.
body.kn: ವಿಶ್ವಗಣ U ಎಂದರೆ ನಾವು ಅಧ್ಯಯನ ಮಾಡುವ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಗಣಗಳನ್ನು ಉಪಗಣಗಳಾಗಿ ಹೊಂದಿರುವ ಮೂಲ ಗಣ.

points.en: Every set under study is a subset of U

explanation.en: The part of A outside B is A − B, the overlap is A ∩ B, the part of B outside A is B − A, and what lies in U but in neither circle is (A ∪ B)′.
explanation.kn: B ಯ ಹೊರಗಿನ A ಭಾಗ A − B, ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಣ A ∩ B, A ಯ ಹೊರಗಿನ B ಭಾಗ B − A, ಎರಡೂ ವೃತ್ತಗಳಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲದ U ಭಾಗ (A ∪ B)′.

body.en: In a Venn diagram $U$ is a rectangle and its subsets are circles inside it. If $A \subset B$, circle $A$ is drawn inside circle $B$. Overlapping circles show common elements; separate circles show sets with no common element.
body.kn: ವೆನ್ ಚಿತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ U ಆಯತ, ಉಪಗಣಗಳು ಅದರೊಳಗಿನ ವೃತ್ತಗಳು. ಒಂದು ವೃತ್ತ ಇನ್ನೊಂದರ ಒಳಗಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದು ಉಪಗಣ.

narration.en: U is a rectangle and subsets are circles inside it. A circle inside another shows a subset; overlapping circles share elements.
narration.kn: ವೆನ್ ಚಿತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ U ಆಯತ, ಉಪಗಣಗಳು ಅದರೊಳಗಿನ ವೃತ್ತಗಳು. ಒಂದು ವೃತ್ತ ಇನ್ನೊಂದರ ಒಳಗಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದು ಉಪಗಣ.

say.en: U is a rectangle and subsets are circles inside it. A circle inside another shows a subset; overlapping circles share elements. Rectangle equals U.

Overlap equals common elements.

caption.en: Fill a Venn diagram from counts: choose n(A), n(B) and n(A ∩ B).

tryThis.en: Set n(A ∩ B) = 0: the circles become disjoint.
Make n(A ∩ B) equal n(B): now B sits inside A.
Can n(A ∩ B) be larger than n(B)? Watch the "only B" bar.

say.en: Fill a Venn diagram from counts: choose nA, nB and nA intersection B.

problem.en: U = {1, 2, …, 10}, A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {4, 6}. Describe the Venn diagram.

steps.en: Every element of B is in A, so B ⊂ A.
Draw circle B inside circle A, both inside rectangle U.
Elements 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 lie in U outside A.

answer.en: B inside A inside U; 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 outside both circles

narration.en: Let us solve this together. U = {1, 2, …, 10}, A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {4, 6}. Describe the Venn diagram.

say.en: Let us solve this together. U = {1, 2,..., 10}, A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {4, 6}. Describe the Venn diagram.
Every element of B is in A, so B is a subset of A.
Draw circle B inside circle A, both inside rectangle U.
Elements 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 lie in U outside A.
So the answer is B inside A inside U; 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 outside both circles.
